doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The jazz and classical schism, including at Roosevelt
summary: Segal says classical and jazz people were divided, recalling a Roosevelt dean who disliked 'jungle music'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did he ever show any sides of having affinity for music outside of opera? Jazz? Did they have any resonance with him? Or was there?
I don’t think so, not like they do now.
Yeah, I was kind of wondering.
There used to be a big schism.
There still is a little bit of a tension point there.

When I first started at Roosevelt there was a schism from the music school. The dean came down one day when we were having our sessions and he said, “They shouldn’t permit that jungle music in this school.”
Yeah. He was a stone Italian opera guy, you know. Staunch, nothing else.
